This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 & 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Apollo Hospital, wherein he took treatment as inpatient, for which he has spent more than Rs.4,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance and nourishment charges.

3. At the time of the accident he was aged about 35 years, hale and healthy, working as coolie,
thereby earning Rs.25,000/- p.m., due to this accident he is completely bed ridden, cannot stand,
walk, sit and squat SCCH-5 and due to severe head injuries, he is suffering from giddiness,
forgotness etc.,
Out of this accident crime No.235/2022 is registered against the driver of the said car before the Basavanagudi Police for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 of IPC.
R1 is the owner, R2 is insurer of the said car, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

Hence,
prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.35,00,000/-.
4. On service of notice, respondent No.1/owner has appeared and filed written statement and denied averments of the petition.

It is submitted that, in FIR date of accident is mentioned as 01.12.2022,
Basavanagudi P.S. Cr.No.235/2022 the incident is mentioned as 08.12.2022 and again the complaint is received on 11.12.2022, which is all created and cooked SCCH-5 story.
Further denied date of occurrence of the alleged accident, lodging of complaint before Basavanagudi Traffic Police.
Further submitted that, petitioner is not entitled for the compensation of Rs.35,00,000/- as claimed by him.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
5. Respondent No.2 being the insurer has filed written statement and denied entire averments of the petition.

He has admitted issuance of policy bearing No.0704003121P112566213 covering the period from 06.03.2022 to 05.03.2023 in respect of car bearing Reg.No.KA-22-N-4940 and liability to pay the compensation is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.

Further submitted that, driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving license and vehicle does not have valid Vishal Jain.R.T vs Vikas Y.J on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107691483/
2 fitness certificate as on the SCCH-5 date of accident.

sentences.text: The petitioner was riding the motor cycle without driving license and without wearing helmet.
There is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act.
Claim made by the petitioner is higher, hence his petition is not maintainable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

6. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1. Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident alleged to have occurred on 11.12.2022 at about 10.45 p.m. due to rash and negligent driving of driver of the Getz Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-LJ-7273?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom?
3.
What order or award?
SCCH-5 7.
In order to prove his case, Petitioner himself deposed his evidence as PW-1, examined Dr.Pradeep .V. is examined as PW-2 and marked 15 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.15 and closed his evidence.
On the other hand, respondents have not chosen to lead evidence.

8. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
 ::REASONS::
9. Issue No.1:-
In order to prove his case, petitioner has deposed his evidence as PW-1, in his chief- SCCH-5 examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in his petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated here.

In this regard he has exhibited copy of FIR with complaint is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of wound certificate is Vishal Jain.R.T vs Vikas Y.J on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107691483/

3 marked as Ex.P.2, copy of mahazar with sketch is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.5.
10.
Further to substantiate the petitioner case, he examined one Doctor as PW-2.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 and his records which was marked as FIR with complaint, mahazar with sketch, IMV Report and charge sheet corroborates the case of the petitioner about causing of the accident dated 08.12.2022 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
SCCH-5 Accordingly the argument addressed by the respondent counsel pertaining to the alleged date of accident is inconsistent, they are all not acceptable one.

11. Per contra, except appearance, filing of written statement, respondents have not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioner about causing of the injuries to the petitioner out of the accident held on 08.12.2022 at about 10.45 p.m. near Vani Vilasa signal, National College Flyouver,
Basavanagudi, Bengaluru.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioner.
SCCH-5 12.
On the other hand, there is no defence evidence and the police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the car driver.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioner, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that,
petitioner has proved the above issue No.1 in his favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:-

As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained deglving over right leg with head injury, abrasion over right side of forehead with hematoma, degloving injury over dorsal aspect of right foot, abrasion over right forearm and left arm and other grievous injuries, for which he has undergone wound debridement right foot, ankle, leg and right forehead with ankle joint capsule repair with extensor tendons of 3rd, 4th SCCH-5 and 5th toes tendos and wound debridement right foot and let with mirovascular free anterolateral thigh flap cover.

In this regard he has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.2, discharge summary marked as Ex.P.8 issued by Apollo Speciality Hospital, wherein he took treatment as indoor patient on 25.08.2023 and 26.08.2023,
medical prescriptions are marked as Ex.P.10, lab reports are marked as Ex.P.11, CD are marked as Ex.P.12.
14.
Dr.Pradeep Y.V. Consultant Plastic Surgeon in Apollo Hospital is examined as PW-2 and he has exhibited copy of MLC record marked as Ex.P.14 and inpatient case file marked as Ex.P.15.

In cross- examination he has categorically admitted that, there was no fracture injuries to the petitioner,
further petitioner requires physiotherapy and there may be SCCH-5 chances of arthritis at the time of old age to the petitioner.
Further he has not assessed the functional disability.

PW-2 Doctor has given assessment of disability i.e., right ankle and toes 30%, right knee 5%, deformity and pain 6%,

15. As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 35 years, for proof of his age, he has produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.6, wherein it is clearly mentioned date of birth of the petitioner is 13.09.1987 and the alleged accident was occurred on SCCH-5 08.12.2022, accordingly relying on Ex.P.6 his age is considered about 36 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 15 is applicable as per decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s.

sentences.text: 16. As per his case, he was working as coolie, thereby earning Rs.25,000/- p.m., to prove the said fact, there are no documents on record.

Under such circumstances, with reference to the year of accident, relying upon the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner is taken at the rate of Rs.14,750/- p.m. so that, said fact is taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss income during laid up period and also for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

It is admitted fact that, as per the discharge summary marked as Ex.P.8, petitioner has admitted in Apollo Hospitals as inpatient on 25.08.2023 and 26.08.2023 i.e., for 2 days.

For the said period he is entitled for the loss of income as per the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner should be taken into consideration i.e., Rs.14,750/- p.m.

sentences.text: Accordingly petitioner is entitled for the income of said quantum for the period he was admitted as inpatient in the hospital.

So petitioner is entitled for Rs.983/- towards loss on income during laid up period.
SCCH-5 18.
Further admittedly he has exhibited Ex.P.9 medical bills for Rs.1,45,990/-.

He also admitted that,  
     .

So as per the admissions of PW-1, out of Rs.1,45,990/-, portion of the amount has been paid by the Medadvantage Insurance Company and only Rs.99,616/- is paid by Vishal Jain.R.T vs Vikas Y.J on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107691483/
5 him.
So for the said medical bills the petitioner is entitled as compensation.

19. Further during the course of arguments, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 vehemently argued SCCH-5 that, petition is filed after two day delay and accident held in junction place, there is also part of negligence on petitioner side and there is no record for occupation of the petitioner and Doctor has not given functional disability etc., but to substantiate the said arguments, there is no evidence on respondent side.
20.

Further on perusal of Ex.P.2 wound certificate in which Doctor who have treated i.e.,
Dr.Shashank B.S. has categorically stated that, petitioner has sustained three grievous injuries out of the accident caused on 08.12.2022.

So as per Ex.P.2 wound certificate, petitioner has abrasion over right side of forehead with hematoma, abrasion over left parieto occipital area, degloving injury over dorsal aspect of righ foot, tendons visible, bleeding and abrasions over right forearm and left arm,
which are grievous in nature.
Further Investigation SCCH-5 Officer has also filed charge sheet against Ashwini S. the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC.

So the said charge sheet materials and evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 clearly states that, petitioner is suffering from grievous injuries out of the accident caused in the alleged accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Accordingly petitioner is entitled for medical expenses of Rs.99,616/-.
21.
Except denial in the written statement, respondents have not taken any endeavors to step into witness box nor to prove the allegations as alleged in the written statement.

In the absence of rebuttal evidence, merely respondents have filed written statement and they have denied entire case of the petitioner are all not sufficient to disbelieve the petitioner case, because it is bounden duty of him to prove the defence as taken in the SCCH-5 written statement.
Except filing of the written statement, cross-examining the PW-1 and PW-2 orally, have not taken any steps to disprove the case of the petitioner.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for medical bills and other compensation as stated below.
22. Accordingly, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-

Sl.No. Head of Compensation Amount in Rs.
1. Loss of Future Income 3,98,250-00 1.
Pain and
sufferings 15,000-00
2. Conveyance, nourishment and 15,000-00 attendant charges 3.
Medical Expenses 99,616-00 4. Loss of amenities in life 15,000-00 5. Loss of income during laid up 983-00 period
Total 5,43,849-00 Vishal Jain.

R.T vs Vikas Y.J on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107691483/
6 23.

Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,43,849/- with SCCH-5 interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

24. In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.0704003121P112566213 which is valid for the period from 06.03.2022 to 05.03.2023, the alleged accident was occurred on 08.12.2022 it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.
Hence naturally liability of R1 shall go against R2, so that, R2/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.

25. Issue No.3: For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
SCCH-5 ::ORDER::
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,43,849/- (Rupees Five Lakhs Forty Three Thousand Eight Hundred Forty Nine Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
SCCH-5 Draw award accordingly.
